title: Workspace Docker capability, isolation and egress enforcement
objective: When the target directory declares Docker dependencies, ./lab and the agent run them predictably and safely: detection and approval at launch, a generated safe compose overlay, workspace labels for teardown, explicit approval for extra context mounts, and enforced egress rules.

acceptance_criteria.text: At launch ./lab detects compose files in the workspace (docker-compose.yml/.yaml, compose.yaml/.yml and override files) and shows them in the existing confirmation summary before anything runs.

A generated override enforces: no published host ports, a workspace-scoped compose project name, com.little-mester.workspace=<path> labels, no privileged mode, no host network/PID/IPC, and no bind mounts outside the workspace.
The agent can run compose commands for the workspace in-session; containers it starts are labelled and removed by ./lab stop, with no orphan containers, volumes or networks left behind.

.mester-egress allowed_domains is enforced by the host-side allowlisting proxy described in §C.8, not advisory: a non-empty list restricts agent egress and image pulls to those domains, and permission=false denies all egress. A blank list keeps the documented allow-all behaviour.

Negative cases are refused with a clear message: published ports, privileged mode, host networking, bind mounts outside the workspace, and pulls from an unapproved registry where policy disallows them.

When the agent needs a host path outside the workspace (for example fixtures or a second checkout), it can request it; ./lab shows the exact path and requires explicit owner approval before mounting it read-only. Nothing outside the workspace is mounted silently.
Mid-session Docker needs (a new image or service) follow an explicit approval step; the agent can write a request but cannot grant it. The flow is documented.
Tests cover the allow/deny matrix, override generation, extra-mount approval and teardown; results are recorded on the ticket.
